cards.text: King David's not done organizing yet. He and the commanders of the army set apart some of the sons of Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun, three Levites David had appointed to serve (1 Chronicles 16:4-5, 41).

cards.question: David and the army commanders set apart some sons of Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun. What are those sons set apart to do?

answers.text: Guard the gates of the city

cards.text: The ARMY commanders helping pick the band? Love it. First up, Asaph's sons: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah and Asarelah, all under the direction of their dad.

cards.question: Asaph's sons work under Asaph. True or false: Asaph himself prophesies under the direction of the king.

cards.text: Next, Jeduthun's six sons, from Gedaliah to Mattithiah, under their father, who prophesies with the harp. Six sons AND a harp in one house? That house was NEVER quiet.

cards.question: Jeduthun prophesies with the harp. What is he doing as he plays?

answers.text: Giving thanks and praise to the LORD
Warning the king about his enemies
Mourning over the sins of the city

cards.text: Then come Heman's sons, and friend, this list does NOT quit. Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, all the way down to Mahazioth. My oven timer went off TWICE.

cards.question: Heman is the king's seer. How were all his sons given to him?

answers.text: Through his service to the king
Through the blessing of his father

cards.question: God gave Heman ___ sons and ___ daughters.
Asaph's sons, Jeduthun's sons and Heman's sons all play cymbals, harps and lyres. What is all that music for?

answers.text: The service of the house of God
The king's court at the palace

cards.text: Seventeen children, Heman? I had six cookie cutters and I thought I was busy. Now add in all their relatives, every one of them trained and skillful in the songs of the LORD.

cards.question: Counting their relatives, the trained and skillful musicians number ___ in all.

cards.text: So who gets which duty? They cast lots, like the office gift swap, just with a LOT more on the line.

cards.question: True or false: When the musicians cast lots for their duties, the teachers got to sit it out.

cards.text: Then the lots fall, twenty-four in all, starting with Joseph from Asaph's family. Every lot is a man, his sons and his brothers, 12 in all, and twenty-four groups of 12 is your 288, right on the dot!

findings.problem: Cards 2, 6, 8, 9 and 12 require facts that cannot be reasoned out from the earlier cards: the sons' ministry, what Jeduthun says while playing, how Heman received his sons, and two exact totals. That makes most of the stop's eight choice cards discovery questions rather than informed guesses.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: Story cards 3, 5, 7 and 11 each contain three sentences. Only the opening story card may exceed two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
